answer: An identity must show a public web presence archived over time: the Wayback Machine must hold snapshots of its site across many months, proving it existed before today. A trellis supports a vine that grows slowly, and an archived site is the same: it cannot be planted yesterday and look old. A pearl forms layer by layer, and so does a credible history: a farm's fresh sites have no snapshots, no depth, nothing to show. A gale of new domains with zero archive history earns nothing until the archive itself vouches for their age.
